findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the user_data script, exposing them to anyone with access to the instance metadata, console, or Terraform state.
The EBS volume does not have the 'encrypted' attribute set to true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and exposed if the underlying storage is compromised.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, exposing potentially sensitive data at rest in the snapshot.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from anywhere on the internet.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) traffic from 0.0.0.0/0, which combined with no encryption exposes traffic and expands the attack surface unnecessarily broad.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to the internet.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, no public access block, and no bucket policy restricting access, risking exposure of sensitive network traffic logs.
